name: buttondown-unsubscribe-to-notion-contact
replaces_classic_zap: Unsubscribe in Buttondown -> Update in Notion

trigger.notes: Polling trigger on the private `Buttondown Unofficial #2` app (source: ~/Repos/zapier-buttondown), the same app that carries `new_email_reschedule` for update-notion-when-rescheduled-in-buttondown. The official ButtondownCLIAPI exposes an `unsubscriber` read, but it is is_hidden and therefore off the stable surface. Durable triggers cannot set a polling interval, so any custom interval on the classic Zap was silently dropped at migration.

connection_notes.notion_wf: work.flowers | Dennis <dennis@work.flowers>. NEVER the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da), which cannot see work.flowers databases.
connection_notes.TableCLIAPI: search/find_record against Zapier Table 01JYEPSEARXB2Z6BJRCMFGXBC2 — Zapier Tables need no connection and cost no tasks.

notion.template_mode: N/A — this updates an existing page and never creates one, so repo rule 5 does not apply

zapier_table.name: Email Addresses <-> Notion Contact Page IDs
zapier_table.result_shape: find_record wraps each hit as {new, old, record_id, table_id} — values at data[0].old.data.<fieldId> — and returns {data: []} on a miss.

fixes_applied_vs_classic_zap: Empty-lookup guard. The classic Zap set `_zap_search_success_on_miss: false`, which halts the Zap on a miss. A durable reading `data[0].old.data.f2` unguarded would instead throw and burn all five step retries. Buttondown holds addresses that were never CRM contacts (site sign-ups, imported lists), so a miss is routine — it now logs and returns `{skipped: "no-notion-contact-for-email"}`.
Lowercases the lookup address. The Table is indexed lowercase by contact-emails-to-zapier-table, so a mixed-case unsubscribe would have missed every row.
A payload with no email_address still throws, naming the keys it received, instead of writing against `undefined`.
Returns only the email and page id rather than the Notion action's echo of the entire contact page, which keeps the step checkpoint small.

verification.main_path: run 019febe7-35e2-7a5c-a373-8bcb57cc1cd2 — nitya@heyamos.com -> contact 04260295-4ab8-4bd2-896c-b28a684d6696, Mailing List written false. Chosen because that contact's Mailing List was ALREADY false, so the write was a no-op against live data.
